title: Little's law, hour by hour
question: Over the hours of one day, does the mean number of NumPy workflow runs in flight equal the hour's arrival rate times its runs' mean time in the system?

issues.text: An hour is not much longer than a typical run, so runs carry load across hour boundaries.
issues.fix: The plan compares hour by hour and over the whole day, where the law is exact.

issues.text: A run's end is not in the data: updated_at is its last update, which a late status change can move hours later.
issues.fix: Runs updated more than 6 h after starting, and re-runs, are left out (the suspect flag).

alternatives.question: Does the whole-day L equal λW exactly?
alternatives.why: The law's exact form: the system is (almost) empty at the window's ends.

alternatives.question: How long do jobs wait for a runner (queue time, from the jobs API)?
alternatives.why: Expand: waiting is what L = λW predicts grows as runners fill up.

hypotheses.statement: Across hours, L measured rises one for one with λW (slope 1, intercept 0).
hypotheses.null: L is unrelated to λW across hours.

concepts.label: Runs in flight
concepts.description: L: runs started and not yet finished, averaged over time.

concepts.label: Arrival rate
concepts.description: λ: runs starting per unit time.

concepts.label: Time in system
concepts.description: W: start to last update, per run.

concepts.label: Runner queue time
concepts.description: Time a job waits for a free runner.
concepts.why: What grows when L nears the runner capacity.

strategy.detail: GitHub jobs API (/actions/runs/{id}/jobs): created_at against started_at per job.

data.request: For each run, its jobs' created_at, started_at and completed_at
data.why: Real end times and the waiting part of W.

method.summary: One row per hour (hourly step); slope and intercept of L on λW, with the whole-day identity (law step) as the exact check.

steps.title: Intervals and L(t)
steps.detail: clean, counted, inflight: arrive_min, depart_min, in_flight per minute.

steps.title: Per hour and per day
steps.detail: hourly: L and lambda_W; law: L_all against lambda_W.

steps.title: Judge the law
steps.detail: Exact over the day; how far per hour, and why.

caveats: updated_at is the run's last update, not the end of its last job.
Runs from the evening before, still running after midnight, are not in the day's list, so the first hours' L is low.
A run is not a runner: one run holds several jobs at once; for runner capacity use jobs.
